question: Describe the approach to reverse a singly linked list in-place.

rubric.logic_context: The list is reversed by iterating once and changing each node's next pointer to point to the previous node using three pointers: previous, current, and next.

concept_groups: store next node before changing pointer
advanced_bonus: saving next node before overwriting pointer is essential — losing it breaks traversal
prev initialized to NULL because the original head becomes the new tail
final return is prev not curr — curr is NULL when loop ends
recursive approach is elegant but uses O(n) call stack space
in-place means O(1) extra space — no new nodes created
handles single-node list and empty list correctly

semantic_targets: Pointers are reversed in-place
No new nodes are created
Original head becomes tail
three pointers are the minimum needed: previous (target), current (working), next (save)
loop invariant: after k iterations, first k nodes are reversed and prev points to the kth node
common_mistakes: Losing the next node reference
Creating a new linked list
Not returning correct new head
forgets to save next pointer before overwriting curr->next — loses rest of list
returns curr instead of prev at the end — curr is NULL after the loop
initializes prev to head instead of NULL — creates a cycle in the reversed list

question: Explain the BFS (Level Order) traversal logic for a binary tree.

rubric.logic_context: BFS traversal processes a binary tree level by level using a queue to ensure nodes are visited in breadth-first order (all nodes at depth d before any node at depth d+1).

advanced_bonus: queue FIFO property ensures level-order — stack would give DFS instead
level separation tracked by recording queue size before processing each level
O(n) time and O(w) space where w is maximum width of tree
worst-case space is O(n/2) for complete binary tree at last level
null nodes should not be enqueued — check before pushing children
can be extended to zigzag level order by alternating direction per level

semantic_targets: Queue enables breadth-first traversal
Nodes are visited level by level
FIFO property maintains correct order
queue FIFO guarantees all nodes at depth d are processed before depth d+1
level separation can be tracked by queue size at start of each level iteration
common_mistakes: Confusing BFS with DFS
Not handling null nodes properly
uses stack instead of queue — gets DFS traversal not BFS
enqueues null children — null pointer dereference when dequeuing
confuses BFS with in-order/pre-order traversal of trees

question: What is a pointer in C and how do you declare one?

mandatory: stores memory address of another variable
advanced_bonus: pointer arithmetic: incrementing by 1 moves by sizeof(type) bytes
void* pointer can hold any address but must be cast before dereferencing
pointer to pointer (**) enables modifying a pointer from a function
NULL pointer should be checked before dereferencing
array name decays to pointer to first element in most expressions

semantic_targets: Pointers refer to memory locations not values
Pointers enable indirect access and modification
& gets address, * dereferences
pointer stores address not value — dereference with * to access the value
common_mistakes: Confusing pointer with the value it points to
Incorrect declaration syntax (int *p vs int* p)
Not initializing pointers before use
declares pointer without initializing — undefined behavior on dereference
confuses * in declaration (pointer type) with * in expression (dereference)
